notes: Agent mini-swe-agent 2.4.6 on both sides, identical prompt (adapter instruction.md, rendered identically), config (step_limit 150, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 = DeepSeek's recommended agentic sampling; default reasoning effort), install (uv, Python 3.12, UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER=2026-10-17T00:00:00Z) and request headers (X-Session-ID). Model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash via the PP API OpenAI-compatible endpoint (requested as deepseek-v4.1-flash; served as deepseek-v4-1-flash-260910). Hardware: one TPU v6e chip (GKE ct6e-standard-1t spot, 1x1), 8 CPU / 32 GiB; 3600 s agent limit; image pins jax/jaxlib 0.12.0, libtpu 0.0.50. Parity split: 15 of the 49 adapted tasks (--split parity: 7 priority kernels + 8 KernelBench-fused). Reward = max(speedup, 1) if correct else 1 (paper's floored speedup); the final /workspace/kernel.py is graded (the paper reports best-so-far over 144 samples, so absolute numbers are not comparable to the paper). Original side: fork's harbor_parity/ runner grading with upstream `python -m JAXBench evaluate`. Infrastructure failures were rerun and excluded: spot preemptions, Harbor agent exec streams dropped by GKE konnectivity-agent scale-downs (fixed by pinning konnectivity replicas), and grading attempts that found the TPU still held by a just-killed process (fixed by retrying the evaluator); every task has one valid result per run on each side (90 total). All metric run-score ranges overlap; per-task disagreements shuffle across runs (e.g. 3p, 4p, 16p, 22k, 46k flip both ways).
